proposal: The Mandate recommends an immediate comprehensive review of all DOJ grant disbursements, including how recipients use funds, and an overhaul of the grant application process with stricter vetting and pre-application eligibility criteria. It also describes how Office of Justice Programs conditions can carry a President's priorities, such as first-term conditions on sharing immigration-status information.

status_summary: DOJ has reviewed its open grants and reshaped award terms and priorities, though no department-wide vetting rule or new pre-application criteria have been published. According to the court's opinion in Vera Institute of Justice v. DOJ (D.D.C., 2025-07-07), DOJ leadership began reviewing about 11,000 open Office of Justice Programs (OJP) awards in February 2025, narrowed the set under active focus to about 2,200 on criteria the government did not disclose, and in April 2025 OJP terminated about 376 discretionary awards to 219 recipients worth more than $820 million, with identical notices citing 2 C.F.R. 200.340(a)(4) (awards no longer advancing agency priorities); a DOJ filing of June 2025, as reported by Law360, describes the same review. Judge Amit Mehta denied a preliminary injunction and dismissed that case on 2025-07-07, and the D.C. Circuit heard the appeal (No. 25-5248) on 2025-10-14 with no opinion found. Executive Order 14332 (signed 2025-08-07) directs agencies to route funding announcements and discretionary awards through senior appointee review, hold annual award reviews and add termination-for-convenience terms, and DOJ is a co-issuer of the Office of Management and Budget proposed rule on federal financial assistance (91 FR 32198, 2026-05-29; comments closed 2026-07-13 with 496,606 received). Section 157 of the continuing appropriations act signed 2026-09-02 (Public Law 119-103, H.R. 6500) bars a rule revising the Uniform Guidance that arises from the proposed rule titled Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance, published 2026-05-29, from being issued or finalized through 2026-12-11. OJP's fiscal year 2025 Justice Assistance Grant notices listed immigration enforcement among four emphasis areas (release of 2026-08-10), and a fiscal year 2026 Bureau of Justice Assistance solicitation for congressionally designated projects (released 2026-06-17) lists immigration law enforcement operations among its priorities and treats programs that impede federal immigration enforcement as out of scope; its risk review and high-risk disclosure are standard OJP application steps rather than new vetting criteria. Twenty states and the District of Columbia sued in August 2025 over immigration conditions on Victims of Crime Act funds and, per a coalition release dated 2026-08-21, amended their complaint to challenge immigration conditions on new law-enforcement and juvenile-justice grants; the coalition says the earlier VOCA conditions were removed. OJP's application guide (dated 2026-09-03) retains a diversity-program certification with a note that DOJ will not enforce it while a court injunction is in effect.

timeline.event: OJP terminates about 376 discretionary awards to 219 recipients worth more than $820 million (April 2025; exact day not given, first of the month used), with identical notices citing 2 C.F.R. 200.340(a)(4); the Vera opinion says DOJ leadership began reviewing about 11,000 open awards in February 2025 and narrowed the set under active focus to about 2,200 on undisclosed criteria. In a motion to dismiss filed 2025-06-09, DOJ says it reviewed more than 11,000 open OJP awards, terminated 376 discretionary grants that no longer effectuated its priorities and plans to reobligate the funds, per Law360.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (via govinfo); Law360

timeline.event: Judge Amit Mehta (D.D.C., Vera Institute of Justice v. DOJ, No. 1:25-cv-01643) denies a preliminary injunction, grants the motion to dismiss and denies class certification as moot: the court finds the APA arbitrary-and-capricious and contrary-to-law claims belong in the Court of Federal Claims under the Tucker Act, rejects the due process claim (no protected property interest in expected grant payments) and dismisses the spending and separation-of-powers and ultra vires claims, while calling the terminations unfair; plaintiffs appeal (D.C. Circuit No. 25-5248) and a narrower stipulated order bars re-obligation of the terminated funds (extended through at least 2026-07-10, per the Clearinghouse).
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (via govinfo)

timeline.event: Executive Order 14332 directs agencies to route funding announcements and discretionary awards through senior appointee review, hold annual reviews of awards and include terms allowing termination for convenience (published 2025-08-12 at 90 FR 38929).

Attorneys general of 20 states and the District of Columbia sue DOJ in federal court in Rhode Island over conditions that would cut Victims of Crime Act funding to recipients that refuse to honor civil immigration enforcement requests, deny ICE access to facilities or withhold advance notice of releases; the report notes no ruling.

The D.C. Circuit hears the appeal in the OJP grant-termination case; per Bloomberg Law, Judge Rao said courts have long treated grants as contracts and the panel appeared skeptical of reviving the cases; no ruling was reported.

The Office of Management and Budget and co-issuing agencies, including DOJ, propose revised federal financial assistance rules covering merit and risk review, award conditions and termination (91 FR 32198); comments closed 2026-07-13 with 496,606 received.

OJP releases a fiscal year 2026 Byrne Discretionary Community Project solicitation (invited applicants only) whose priorities include supporting law enforcement operations, including immigration law enforcement operations; it treats programs that impede federal immigration enforcement or unlawfully favor groups by race as out of scope, bars funds for legal services to removable aliens with exceptions, and requires risk-review disclosures.

A coalition of attorneys general (Michigan's release of this date) announces an amended complaint challenging immigration-enforcement conditions DOJ applied to new public safety grants this year, including Byrne JAG, as violating the APA and the Spending Clause; the release does not name the court and reports no ruling. OJP's 2026-08-10 release had named immigration enforcement among four fiscal year 2025 JAG emphasis areas.

The President approves Public Law 119-103 (H.R. 6500, Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027; approved 2026-09-02; funding through 2026-12-11). Section 157 of Division A bars a rule revising the Uniform Guidance for federal awards that arises from the proposed rule titled Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance (published 2026-05-29), or a substantially similar rule, from being issued or finalized through 2026-12-11 and from taking effect if issued earlier.

title: Review DOJ grants and tighten applicant vetting and award conditions
uncertainties: The review of open OJP awards is now documented in the district court's opinion (read through a fetch summary) and, from DOJ's side, by Law360's report of its June 2025 filing; the filing itself and any review memo were not read, and whether the review examined recipients' use of funds, as the Mandate specifies, is not established. The Mandate's call for stricter pre-application vetting is met only in part (invitation-only eligibility and risk disclosures in one solicitation). The court gives April 2025 for the terminations without a day, and counts differ between the opinion (about 376 awards to 219 recipients, more than $820 million) and the Clearinghouse page (more than 370 awards). The D.C. Circuit appeal (No. 25-5248) was argued 2025-10-14; an opinion could not be found (the court's site could not be searched and the web search budget is exhausted), so the appeal's outcome is unknown a year later and the Clearinghouse page's last-update date is unclear. The en banc August 2026 climate-grant decision (Climate United v. Citibank) was not tied to the DOJ case. The state immigration-condition suits come from press releases (PBS for 2025-08-18; Michigan's release for 2026-08-21), the court of the 2026 amended complaint is not named, and an earlier Rhode Island press release surfaced in search concerned 2018 conditions and was not used. OJP's resource guide (2026-09-03) and the 2026-08-10 JAG release, the Law360 report and the Federal Register record of 91 FR 32198 were carried forward from earlier reviews and not refetched. Public Law 119-103's section 157 identifies the barred rule by its title and publication date (2026-05-29), not by Federal Register citation, which matches the OMB rule DOJ co-issued. The injunction behind the diversity certification note was not identified.
